output.title: Customer-facing web app returning 5xx errors
output.symptoms: Customers report that a customer-facing application, such as the Customer Portal, returns 500/502/503 errors, or synthetic monitors fail.
output.cause: A bad deployment, exhausted connection pools, failing downstream dependencies, or autoscaling hitting its maximum instance count during a traffic spike.
steps: Check the deployment history. If a release happened within the last 24 hours, consider rolling back first.
Review application logs and APM traces for the failing endpoint.
Check instance counts against autoscaling limits, and check database connection pool metrics.
If instances are at the autoscaling maximum, raise the max instance limit.
Add a CPU-based scaling policy so the app scales out earlier during traffic spikes.
Post customer communication through the status page if the outage lasts more than 15 minutes.
output.rationale: KB0010026 already lists autoscaling limits as a cause but only says to check instance counts, so it is updated with the fix: raising the max instance limit and adding a CPU-based scaling policy.
KB0010025 already covers stale reporting data from replication lag, including IO saturation on the replica and pausing maintenance jobs, which is exactly how this incident was resolved.

KB0010024 already covers report queries timing out due to a missing index after table growth, including checking missing index recommendations and creating a change request for new indexes, which matches this fix.
KB0010023 already covers a blocked invoice caused by a closed posting period and the fix of opening the period in OB52 after finance confirms, which is how this incident was resolved.
KB0010021 already documents month-end batch jobs competing with interactive users and the fix applied here (rescheduling non-critical batch jobs and adding dialog work processes).

KB0010022 already documents a PO stuck in the SAP release workflow due to an errored workitem from a missing cost center, with the fix of correcting master data and restarting the workflow, which is exactly how this incident was resolved.
KB0010012 already lists a failing dock power supply as a cause and dock replacement as the fix, which is exactly how this incident was resolved.

KB0010011 already covers BitLocker recovery prompts and blue screens at boot caused by motherboard failure, including the vendor diagnostics, loaner, warranty case and OneDrive restore that resolved this incident.

KB0010010 already covers slow laptops with a constantly running fan caused by low disk space from the OneDrive cache, and its first step (enable Files On-Demand and clear temp files) is exactly the fix applied.

KB0010032 already covers failed MDM enrollment caused by an OS version below the compliance policy, and its steps (check the compliance reason, update the OS, re-check status) match how this incident was fixed; the close notes say iOS although the caller reported an Android phone, but the fix is the same either way.

output.headline: Handheld scanners at Memphis DC failed to sync with the WMS on 2026-08-18 because their Wi-Fi certificates had expired.
output.impact: 60 hardware/handheld tickets came in from Memphis DC, about 60 times the normal rate of 0.89 a day. The incident ran 25.6 h from the first ticket at 2026-08-18 06:22 to the last resolution at 2026-08-19 07:59; the worst priority was 3 - Moderate, with 0 SLA breaches and an average resolution time of 16.8 h.
timeline: 06:22 - First ticket: handheld scanner HH-ATL-032 at Memphis DC not syncing.
12:00 - Ticket arrivals peak at 6 in the hour, including reports of RF guns freezing and scanners failing to connect to the WMS.
22:45 - Last sampled report of scans not uploading from a handheld (HH-ATL-190); ticket arrivals had continued every hour since 06:00.

output.title: Exchange Online vendor service incident disrupted mail flow across all Meridian sites (week of 2026-01-19)
output.problem_statement: During the week of 2026-01-19, users at Atlanta DC, Chicago HQ, Dallas DC, Memphis DC, Remote and Toronto Office reported Outlook not receiving email, not syncing, stuck on 'Updating' or disconnected, driven by an Exchange Online service incident linked to major incident MI20260120-email. The surge produced 150 email tickets against a baseline of 7.75 per week (about 142 above baseline), consuming 680.8 resolution hours with 1 SLA breach.
output.root_cause_hypothesis: High confidence: a vendor-side Exchange Online service incident impaired mail flow. The same fix ('Exchange Online service incident affected mail flow. Resolved after vendor mitigation') resolved 95% of surge tickets, compared with 33% of this subcategory's tickets outside surges. Volume returned to baseline the following week, which fits a single external outage rather than an internal configuration fault. The data does not show the vendor's own root cause. It also does not show why individual tickets were held open for hours awaiting vendor mitigation.
evidence: 150 tickets in the week of 2026-01-19, against a 7.75/week baseline and 5 tickets the following week.
The Exchange Online service incident fix resolved 95% of surge tickets, against 33% outside surges.
680.8 resolution hours and 1 SLA breach. Sample tickets took 3.1–6.8 h each, all closing around 12:36–13:25 on 2026-01-20, consistent with waiting on vendor mitigation.
Six sites were affected, all resolved by Messaging & Collaboration and linked to major incident MI20260120-email.
output.workaround: The service desk linked each ticket to the parent incident (MI20260120-email). Tickets were held until Microsoft's mitigation restored mail flow, then closed. Some agents also followed KB0010015. Where symptoms persisted afterwards (for example, 2026-01-24 Dallas DC), a corrupted OST file was fixed by rebuilding the Outlook profile and resyncing the mailbox.
output.permanent_fix: The outage itself was vendor-side and cannot be prevented internally. The change needed is to reduce its impact on Meridian: proactively monitor Microsoft 365 Service Health and alert on Exchange Online incidents, and issue rapid user communications such as banners, IVR messages or status pages to deflect duplicate tickets. A mass-link/bulk-close process for child tickets would cut the hours spent, and a follow-up check would catch residual OST/profile corruption after recovery.
next_steps: Hold a post-incident review of MI20260120-email: obtain Microsoft's post-incident report, confirm the vendor root cause, and review the SLA breach and time to detect.
Raise a change request to integrate Microsoft 365 Service Health alerts for Exchange Online into the monitoring and alerting platform.
Update KB0010015 with outage-specific guidance: how to identify vendor incidents, link and bulk-resolve child tickets, and rebuild the Outlook profile if sync fails after recovery.
Create a major-incident communication template to post a status notice early and deflect duplicate email tickets during vendor outages.

output.title: GlobalProtect client upgrade leaves corrupted cached portal configuration, blocking remote VPN access
output.problem_statement: Since the week of 2026-05-04, remote users have repeatedly been unable to connect to VPN because the new GlobalProtect client version is running with a corrupted cached portal configuration, with symptoms including timeouts, login failures, portal certificate errors and disconnects. Over the six-week surge to the week of 2026-06-08, 135 tickets were raised (about 100 above the 5.83/week baseline), consuming 1,088 resolution hours and causing 6 SLA breaches.
output.root_cause_hypothesis: The rollout of the new GlobalProtect client version is most likely corrupting or failing to migrate the cached portal settings on remote endpoints, so the client cannot reach or authenticate to the portal until the cache is cleared and the portal address re-entered. Confidence is high: this single fix resolved 100% of surge tickets against 34% of this subcategory's tickets outside surges, and the surge starts abruptly in one week. The data does not show the upgrade date, the exact version or the mechanism of corruption, so these still need confirming.
evidence: Weekly volume jumped from 2 tickets (weeks of 2026-04-20 and 2026-04-27) to 23 in the week of 2026-05-04, and stayed at 19-25 a week through the week of 2026-06-08.
The cached-portal-config fix resolved 100% of the 135 surge tickets, compared with 34% of this subcategory's tickets outside surges.
The surge consumed 1,088 resolution hours with 6 SLA breaches; sample resolution times ranged from 0.7 h to 19.4 h.
All tickets came from Remote users and were resolved by Network Operations; volume eased to 11 in the week of 2026-06-15 and returned to 4-9 a week afterwards.
output.workaround: Network Operations clears the GlobalProtect client's cached portal settings, re-enters the portal address and confirms the VPN connects, following KB0010006.
output.permanent_fix: Fix the GlobalProtect upgrade package or deployment so the portal configuration is reset or correctly migrated during the upgrade, for example by pushing the portal address by policy or clearing the cached portal settings as part of the install. output.title: Recurring WAN/internet slowness from degraded proxy pool nodes and business-hours backup jobs saturating site WAN circuits
output.problem_statement: From the week of 2026-07-06 through the week of 2026-07-20, users at Atlanta DC, Chicago HQ, Dallas DC, Memphis DC and Toronto Office repeatedly reported slow internet and website browsing, raising 18 network/WAN tickets against a baseline of 1.75 a week (about 13 above baseline). These tickets took 268.8 resolution hours for Network Operations, with no SLA breaches.
output.root_cause_hypothesis: The evidence for a single root cause is weak. The dominant fix, removing a degraded proxy node from the pool per KB0010009, resolved only 44% of surge tickets. That is less than its 57% share outside surges, so it is a long-standing recurring fix rather than the driver of the surge. The sample tickets point to a second, newer cause from mid-July: large backup jobs running during business hours saturated the WAN circuits at Toronto Office and Dallas DC, and four of the eight samples were fixed by rescheduling the job. The most likely explanation is two overlapping causes. The first is chronic proxy node degradation with no automated health-based removal. The second is backup jobs scheduled, or newly moved, into business hours. Confidence is moderate for the backup contribution to the late-July peak and low for any single cause.
evidence: Weekly volume rose from a 1.75/week baseline to 5, 5 and 8 tickets in the weeks of 2026-07-06, 07-13 and 07-20, then fell back to 1 in the week of 2026-07-27.
The proxy-node removal fix (KB0010009) resolved 44% of surge tickets versus 57% of tickets outside surges, so it does not explain the increase.
4 of the 8 sample tickets, at Toronto Office and Dallas DC between 2026-07-15 and 2026-07-24, were resolved by rescheduling a large business-hours backup job that saturated the WAN circuit.
The 18 surge tickets consumed 268.8 resolution hours, and individual samples took up to 30.2 h to resolve.
output.workaround: Network Operations finds the degraded proxy node and removes it from pool rotation following KB0010009, which restores browsing speed. Where a site's WAN circuit is saturated, they identify the large backup job running during business hours and reschedule it to off-hours.
output.permanent_fix: Add automated health checks to the proxy pool so degraded nodes are pulled from rotation without a ticket, and find and fix the reason nodes degrade. Enforce a backup scheduling policy, backed by QoS or bandwidth limits on the WAN links, so large backup jobs cannot run over site WAN circuits during business hours.
next_steps: Raise a change request to configure automated health-check-based removal of degraded nodes in the proxy pool, and investigate the recurring cause of node degradation.
Review backup job schedules at Toronto Office, Dallas DC and other sites, and raise a change to lock large jobs to off-hours windows with bandwidth throttling or QoS on the WAN.
Create monitoring alerts for proxy node latency and error rates and for WAN circuit utilization above a threshold during business hours.
Update KB0010009 and add a KB article for diagnosing WAN saturation caused by backups, so the desk can tell the two causes apart quickly and cut the 4–30 h resolution times.
